def score(f, p, hw, w):
    # Width-1 raster the tie-break below realises (current contract cannot see swizzle): along the shorter grid side.
    # M<=N: identity (M-fastest), A panels are the fast-dim panels; M>N: horizontal (N-fastest), B panels are.
    if p.M > p.N:
        d = f.dram_w1_hz_ratio
        sgn = 1.0
    else:
        d = f.dram_w1_id_ratio
        sgn = -1.0
    # DRAM leg: ONE consistent byte count for that raster, including split-K partials and spills.
    sm = np.maximum(f.tm_crit_ratio, f.tm_l2_ratio)
    t = np.sqrt(np.square(sm) + np.square(d))
    s = 10.0 * np.log2(t)
    # Efficiency the norm cannot see: register-staged 2-stage mainloop, CTA-wide barrier over more warps.
    s = s + w[0] * f.tm_regstaged + w[1] * f.tm_cta_warps
    # Split-K time model with an interior optimum, in log2 time.
    s = s + w[2] * f.splitk_roofline_log_time
    # A long reduction exposes the accumulated loop-control and synchronization cost.
    # Log compression keeps the absolute iteration count commensurate with the time-model score.
    if p.log_min_dim < 8:
        # Short-dimension shapes have little steady-state pipeline to amortize fill/drain latency.
        s = s + w[3] * np.log2(f.mainloop_iteration_count)
        s = s + w[4] * f.pipeline_fill_drain_fraction
    else:
        # On long reductions, repeated per-iteration overhead dominates the fixed prologue/epilogue fraction.
        s = s + w[5] * np.log2(f.mainloop_iteration_count)
        s = s + w[6] * f.pipeline_fill_drain_fraction
    # Pure tie-break among raster variants that differ only in inst_total; sign fixed by physics (shorter-side raster).
    s = s + 0.001 * sgn * f.tm_log_inst
    return s

def score(f, p, hw, w):
    # Width-1 raster the tie-break below realises (current contract cannot see swizzle): along the shorter grid side.
    # M<=N: identity (M-fastest), A panels are the fast-dim panels; M>N: horizontal (N-fastest), B panels are.
    if p.M > p.N:
        d = f.dram_w1_hz_ratio
        sgn = 1.0
    else:
        d = f.dram_w1_id_ratio
        sgn = -1.0
    # DRAM leg: ONE consistent byte count for that raster (pool feature dram_w1_*): panels fetched once per one-CTA-per-SM
    # K-lockstep window (whole grid if co-resident in one round), re-fetched across windows unless the reuse distance fits L2,
    # plus C write, split-K partials, spills; DRAM time / ideal compute time.
    sm = np.maximum(f.tm_crit_ratio, f.tm_l2_ratio)
    t = np.sqrt(np.square(sm) + np.square(d))
    s = 10.0 * np.log2(t)
    # Efficiency the norm cannot see: register-staged 2-stage mainloop, CTA-wide barrier over more warps.
    s = s + w[0] * f.tm_regstaged + w[1] * f.tm_cta_warps
    # Split-K time model with an interior optimum, in log2 time.
    s = s + w[2] * f.splitk_roofline_log_time
    # Pure tie-break among raster variants that differ only in inst_total: shorter-side raster.
    s = s + 0.001 * sgn * f.tm_log_inst
    # In populated, non-skinny grids, a short tile_k exposes loop iterations; price that
    # against the tile's bandwidth deficit and the residency cost of the larger tile.
    if p.log_min_dim > 6 and p.output_work_per_sm > 1024:
        s = s + w[3] * (np.log2(f.mainloop_iteration_count) * (1.0 + f.tile_roofline_deficit))
        s = s + w[4] * f.shared_memory_pressure
        s = s + w[5] * f.resident_block_scarcity
        s = s + w[6] * f.wave_count_deficit
    return s

def score(f, p, hw, w):
    # Width-1 raster tie-break: use the shorter-grid-side raster and its consistent DRAM model.
    if p.M > p.N:
        d = f.dram_w1_hz_ratio
        sgn = 1.0
    else:
        d = f.dram_w1_id_ratio
        sgn = -1.0
    # The SM feed and compute paths overlap; DRAM remains an imperfect-overlap leg.
    sm = np.maximum(f.tm_crit_ratio, f.tm_l2_ratio)
    t = np.sqrt(np.square(sm) + np.square(d))
    s = 10.0 * np.log2(t)
    # Efficiency corrections retained from the parent.
    s = s + w[0] * f.tm_regstaged + w[1] * f.tm_cta_warps
    s = s + w[2] * f.splitk_roofline_log_time
    # Keep the established shorter-side raster tie-break.
    s = s + 0.001 * sgn * f.tm_log_inst
    # A small output surface has too little useful work per CTA to be described by
    # the aggregate time norm alone.  GEMV-like shapes are especially boundary- and
    # thread-overhead-sensitive, whereas less-rectangular low-work shapes are more
    # limited by resident resources and dispatch waves.
    if p.output_work_per_sm < 1024.0:
        if p.output_aspect_imbalance > 0.8:
            s = s + w[3] * f.thread_work_granularity_deficit
            s = s + w[4] * np.log2(1.0 + f.edge_waste)
            s = s + w[5] * f.register_file_pressure
            s = s + w[6] * f.resident_block_scarcity
            s = s + w[7] * f.wave_count_deficit
        else:
            s = s + w[8] * f.thread_work_granularity_deficit
            s = s + w[9] * np.log2(1.0 + f.edge_waste)
            s = s + w[10] * f.register_file_pressure
            s = s + w[11] * f.resident_block_scarcity
            s = s + w[12] * f.wave_count_deficit
    return s
